note: The rules of Tennis Tipping as they stand today, and how they have changed over the years.

items: Rankings run over a rolling 52 weeks: points drop off exactly 52 weeks after they were won.
A player's best 18 events count, and the four Grand Slams always count.
The year-end Finals counts as a 19th event.
The Hopman Cup and WTC Dusseldorf don't give ranking points.
Doubles rankings follow the same rules, with the points going to each player of the team.
A list is posted every Monday the ATP publishes its rankings. There is no cut-off: everyone with an event in the past 52 weeks is listed.
First, the most points from Grand Slam, Masters 1000 and World Tour Finals main draws.
Then the fewest events played, counting missed Grand Slams the player could have played.
Then the highest points from a single tournament, then the second highest, and so on.
A lucky loser is a player who lost in the last round of qualifying. An alternate (ALT) can also come in as a lucky loser.
Futures carry the same points as Challengers and are counted with them, along with other events that aren't on the ATP calendar.
The NextGen Finals counts as a Challenger event.

history.text: The rankings were frozen from 16 March to 24 August 2020. Weeks in the freeze don't count towards weeks at no. 1 or in the top 10.
The ranking points used from 2007 to 2010 weren't recorded, and the points table has changed since. The site's lists for those seasons are estimates rebuilt from the results.
